description: One introduced fish wiped out more than 200 species in Lake Victoria. Biologists call it one of the biggest vertebrate extinctions ever caused by a single introduction. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow
script: In the 1950s, people introduced the Nile perch to Lake Victoria to boost fishing. It ate its way through the lake's cichlids, and more than two hundred species disappeared. The big fish now fuel a major export industry. But local fishermen say the fish are too oily to dry in the sun, so forests are burned to smoke them. Biologists call it one of the biggest vertebrate extinctions ever caused by a single introduction.

title: Purple sea urchins have turned kelp forests into barren rock #shorts
description: Purple sea urchins have turned kelp forests into barren rock. Scientists and divers now smash urchins by hand, trying to give the kelp a chance to return. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow
script: Off the California coast, ninety-five percent of the kelp forest is gone. A sea star disease killed the predators that kept purple urchins in check, and the urchin population exploded. They eat every blade of kelp, and they can survive starving for years. What was once an underwater forest is now gray rock. Scientists and divers now smash urchins by hand, trying to give the kelp a chance to return.

title: Ebola killed thousands of gorillas in a few years #shorts
description: Ebola killed thousands of gorillas in a few years. Poaching and habitat loss have since pushed the western gorilla to critically endangered status. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow
script: Ebola killed thousands of western gorillas in a few short years. The outbreak around 2002 swept through the forests of Central Africa, wiping out most of some gorilla groups. Gorillas are social animals that groom each other, so the virus spread fast. Their numbers recover slowly, because females give birth only once every four years. Poaching and habitat loss have since pushed the western gorilla to critically endangered status.

title: A virus killed up to 90 percent of cattle in Africa in the 1890s #shorts
description: A virus killed up to 90 percent of cattle in Africa in the 1890s. Researchers say the famine reshaped the African landscape, as open grazing land turned into thick bush. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow
script: In the 1890s, a virus called rinderpest swept through Africa and killed up to ninety percent of the cattle. Wildebeest and buffalo died too. Without cattle, many pastoral peoples starved. Humans eventually wiped out the disease on purpose, and in 2011 rinderpest became only the second virus ever eradicated. Researchers say the famine reshaped the African landscape, as open grazing land turned into thick bush.

title: DDT made eggshells so thin that parents crushed their own chicks #shorts
description: DDT made eggshells so thin that parents crushed their own chicks. Today they nest on skyscrapers in major cities, the fastest animals on Earth. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow
script: DDT nearly wiped out the peregrine falcon. The pesticide built up in the food chain and made the birds' eggshells so thin that they cracked under the weight of the parent. By the 1960s, the peregrine had disappeared east of the Mississippi. After DDT was banned in 1972, careful breeding and release brought them back. Today they nest on skyscrapers in major cities, the fastest animals on Earth.
